title: Embedded resources
description: A tool result block that inlines a resource's contents together with its URI and MIME type.
question: Does an embedded resource keep its identity, or arrive as anonymous text?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: The URI and MIME type are what let a caller cite, cache or re-read the content. Stripping them to the inner text leaves the agent holding data it cannot attribute to a source.

notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: the whole embedded resource is re-serialized as JSON inside a text item. The `uri` and `mimeType` survive as characters, so the resource is still identifiable if the agent parses the text.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: only the resource's text is returned, as a bare string. The `uri` and `mimeType` are gone, so the agent cannot tell this came from a resource at all.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: a result without `structuredContent` comes back unchanged, embedded resource intact with its `uri` and `mimeType`. For a result that carries `structuredContent`, every content block is dropped, embedded resources included; only the structured value reaches the agent.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): execute resolves with the CallToolResult, so a caller reading a step's toolResults gets the embedded resource block intact. The adapter's toModelOutput converter maps only text and image blocks, so the model receives an embedded resource block as a text part holding the block's JSON (the uri and contents as characters). Boundary-dependent: kept at execute, flattened to text at model_output.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: An embedded text resource becomes a bare `{"text": ...}` item (and a blob becomes text or an image by MIME type). The resource's `uri` and `mimeType` are dropped, so the model cannot tell the content came from a resource. The upstream code carries a TODO about exactly this.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the model receives an embedded resource as its JSON serialization inside a text item; `MCPServer.callTool` itself returns the block intact.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: an embedded resource becomes the text `[Embedded resource: <resource JSON>]` at both boundaries: the contents survive as characters, not as a resource block.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: with the default `result_mode="text"`, `Tool.acall` returns the embedded resource block as the MCP content object when the result has no text (direct: `y`). In a `dspy.ReAct` run the observation the model reads is that object's Python repr, `«type='resource' resource=TextResourceContents(...)»` (react: `a`). When a result carries any text block, `_convert_mcp_tool_result` returns the text alone and drops the embedded resource block at both boundaries.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): an embedded `resource` block goes into the artifact only. The `ToolMessage` content the model reads is `[]`, and `tool.invoke` returns `[]`.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): depends on the boundary. `agent`: the `tool` message holds only the resource's text (`SENTINEL_EMBEDDED_RESOURCE`); its `uri` and `mimeType` are dropped. `direct`: `session.rpc.tools.execute` returns the `resource` block whole.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: The default `McpToolExecutor` result converter accepts text blocks only. Any embedded `resource` block makes it throw `Unsupported content type: "resource"`: the direct executor raises it as a `RuntimeException`, and AiServices turns it into an error tool result the model reads in place of the block. A result with `structuredContent` never reads its blocks at all.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcpTool.Run` returns `{"output": text}`, where `formatMCPContent` replaces the block with a placeholder line (`[MCP embedded resource: uri=..., mimeType=...]` followed by the text), and the model receives that map as `FunctionResponse.response`. When the result also has `structuredContent`, as in the mixed result, `Run` returns `{"output": structuredContent}` and the block is dropped.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): an embedded text `resource` becomes a `TextContent` holding only the resource's text (`SENTINEL_EMBEDDED_RESOURCE`); its `uri` and `mimeType` are dropped at both boundaries. Beside `structuredContent` (`mixed_content`) the block survives only inside the `CallToolResult` JSON text.

summary: An embedded resource carries its own identity: a uri, a mime type, and contents.
